Ensures file-level @supports via ensureFileSupportsAnnotation(context, sourceCode, {...}) (REQ-TEST-FILE-SUPPORTS). - Builds describeRegex from describePattern and passes it, along with requireDescribeStory/requireTestReqPrefix flags, into handleCallExpression, which is wired as the CallExpression visitor. ,Helper implementation: src/rules/helpers/require-test-traceability-helpers.ts - JSDoc shows linkage to 020.0 requirements: - "@supports docs/stories/020.0-DEV-TEST-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION.story.md REQ-TEST-PATTERN-DETECT REQ-TEST-FRAMEWORK-COMPAT" - "@supports docs/stories/020.0-DEV-TEST-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION.story.md REQ-TEST-FILE-SUPPORTS REQ-TEST-SUPPORTS-VALID" (for ensureFileSupportsAnnotation) - REQ-TEST-DESCRIBE-STORY REQ-TEST-IT-REQ-PREFIX REQ-TEST-NESTED-DESCRIBE REQ-TEST-ERROR-CONTEXT" (for handleCallExpression) - Test file detection (REQ-TEST-PATTERN-DETECT): - determineIsTestFile(filename, rawPatterns): returns true if filename includes any of ["/tests/", "/test/", "/__tests__", ".test.", ".spec."] after minor normalization. This matches the Implementation Notes for directory/extension-based detection and is configurable via rule options. - File-level @supports validation & auto-fix (REQ-TEST-FILE-SUPPORTS, REQ-TEST-SUPPORTS-VALID when combined with existing rules): - ensureFileSupportsAnnotation(context, sourceCode, autoFixOptions): - Collects all comments via sourceCode.getAllComments(). - fileHasSupports = ANY comment whose value matches /@supports\b/. - If missing, reports messageId "missingFileSupports" on either the first comment or Program node. - When autoFixTestTemplate is not false, it uses insertSupportsTemplate() to insert a placeholder multi-line JSDoc at the top of the file with a default `@supports docs/stories/XXX.X-STORY-NAME.story.md REQ-XXX-YYY REQ-XXX-ZZZ` template and a TODO line. - This guarantees presence of @supports; validity of story paths and REQ IDs is then enforced by existing rules valid-story-reference and valid-req-reference (dependencies 006.0 and 010.0), satisfying REQ-TEST-SUPPORTS-VALID in combination with prior work. - Test framework compatibility (REQ-TEST-FRAMEWORK-COMPAT): - isTestCallName(name): returns true for ["describe", "it", "test", "context"]. - getCalleeName handles both simple identifiers and MemberExpressions (e.g., describe.each, test.only), ensuring compatibility with Jest-specific patterns. - Describe block validation (REQ-TEST-DESCRIBE-STORY, REQ-TEST-NESTED-DESCRIBE): - handleCallExpression(context, options) registers a CallExpression visitor that: - Resolves calleeName; returns early if not a known test function. - Extracts first argument string literal via getFirstArgumentLiteral. - For calleeName === "describe", delegates to handleDescribeCall, which: - if requireDescribeStory is true and describeRegex does not match description, reports messageId "missingDescribeStory". - As every describe() in a test file is visited (no restriction to top-level), both top-level and nested describe blocks are validated according to the same pattern, satisfying "handle nested describe() blocks appropriately" by choosing the "all levels" behavior. - Test name requirement prefixes & error context (REQ-TEST-IT-REQ-PREFIX, REQ-TEST-ERROR-CONTEXT): - handleItOrTestCall(context, node, description, options): - If requireTestReqPrefix is true and description does not match /^\[REQ-[^\]]+]/, it reports messageId "missingReqPrefix". - When autoFixTestPrefixFormat is enabled, it attempts to normalize malformed REQ prefixes with normalizeReqPrefixInDescription, covering multiple malformed forms while preserving semantics: - "[ REQ-XXX ]...", "[REQ_XXX]...", "(REQ-XXX)...", "[req-xxx]...". - createUpdatedStringLiteralRaw preserves existing quote style and escaping, aligning with ESLint best-practice for auto-fixers. - The error messages themselves are clear and include concrete examples (e.g., "(e.g., '[REQ-MAINT-DETECT] ...')"), providing actionable context even though the exact missing ID cannot be known. - handleCallExpression applies handleItOrTestCall only for "it" and "test" callees; this ensures Jest/Mocha-style tests are validated consistently while leaving framework grouping functions like describe/context to their intended roles. ,Tests for rule behavior: tests/rules/require-test-traceability.test.ts - File header: - "Tests for: docs/stories/020.0-DEV-TEST-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION.story.md" and story 021.0. - @supports annotations include REQ-TEST-FILE-SUPPORTS, REQ-TEST-DESCRIBE-STORY, REQ-TEST-IT-REQ-PREFIX, REQ-TEST-FRAMEWORK-COMPAT, REQ-TEST-PATTERN-DETECT, and 021.0 auto-fix requirements. - Valid cases: - REQ-TEST-FILE-SUPPORTS: A file with file-level @supports and both describe + it fully satisfying conventions is accepted: - Code includes a top-of-file JSDoc with `@supports docs/stories/020.0-... REQ-TEST-FILE-SUPPORTS` and `describe('Story 020.0-DEV-TEST-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION', ...)` plus `it('[REQ-EXAMPLE] does something', ...)`. - REQ-TEST-FRAMEWORK-COMPAT: Mocha-style `context('Story 020.0-DEV-TEST-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION', () => {});` with file-level @supports is accepted, proving correct handling of alternative test framework naming. - REQ-TEST-PATTERN-DETECT: A file named `src/not-a-test-file.ts` with describe + @supports is treated as a non-test file and therefore ignored by the rule, verifying that only matching paths (tests/, .test., etc.) are subject to validation. - REQ-TEST-FIX-PREFIX-FORMAT (from story 021.0): Already-correct `[REQ-TRACE-123]` prefix remains unchanged under auto-fix, showing no-op behavior on valid inputs. - Invalid cases: - REQ-TEST-FILE-SUPPORTS: Missing file-level @supports in a test file: - Input: `describe('Story 020.0-DEV-TEST-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION', ...);` without any @supports. - Expected: error with `messageId: "missingFileSupports"` and an auto-fixed output inserting the placeholder @supports template at the top of the file. - REQ-TEST-DESCRIBE-STORY: describe() without story reference: - Input has @supports but describe('no story reference here', ...). - Expected: error with `messageId: "missingDescribeStory"`. No auto-fix is attempted (as expected per story). - REQ-TEST-IT-REQ-PREFIX and REQ-TEST-FIX-NO-INFERENCE: it() call with description 'missing prefix' causes a `missingReqPrefix` error with no auto-fix (no REQ is present to normalize). - REQ-TEST-FIX-PREFIX-FORMAT: three malformed REQ prefixes are normalized by auto-fix while reporting `missingReqPrefix`: - '[ REQ-TEST-FIX ] does something' -> '[REQ-TEST-FIX] does something'. - '[REQ_TEST_FIX] does something' -> '[REQ-TEST-FIX] does something'. - '[req-lowercase] bad casing' -> '[REQ-LOWERCASE] bad casing'. - '(REQ-PAREN) with parens' -> '[REQ-PAREN] with parens'. - These tests, run through ESLint's RuleTester, confirm correct behavior for file-level annotations, describe story references, REQ-prefixed test names, basic framework compatibility (describe/it/context), and non-test file detection. ,Plugin integration and configuration: src/index.ts and tests - src/index.ts: - RULE_NAMES includes "require-test-traceability" alongside other core rules, enabling dynamic loading. - TRACEABILITY_RULE_SEVERITIES maps "traceability/require-test-traceability" to "error". - createTraceabilityFlatConfig returns a rules map spreading TRACEABILITY_RULE_SEVERITIES into flat config presets. - configs.recommended and configs.strict both include this rule with severity "error". - tests/plugin-default-export-and-configs.test.ts: - Verifies that rules contain "require-test-traceability" in the exported rule list. - Asserts that configs.recommended maps "traceability/require-test-traceability" to "error". - Verifies strict config uses the same rules and severities as recommended. - tests/config/flat-config-presets-integration.test.ts: - Uses FlatESLint with plugin configs.recommended/strict and confirms rules are enabled correctly. While this test focuses on require-story-annotation, the underlying configs include require-test-traceability as shown above, confirming integration into the standard config pipeline. - Combined, this demonstrates that the rule is fully integrated with the plugin's dynamic rule loading, recommended/strict configurations, and thus will run for consumer projects using those presets (Integration AC met). ,Documentation evidence - README.md: - Lists the rule with a clear behavioral summary: - "traceability/require-test-traceability Enforces traceability conventions in test files by requiring file-level `@supports` annotations, story references in `describe` blocks, and `[REQ-...]` prefixes in `it`/`test` names. (See the rule documentation in the plugin's user guide.)" - This directly documents the core behavior specified in the story (file-level @supports, describe story reference, REQ-prefixed test names) and indicates more detailed documentation exists in the user guide. - Rule & helper JSDoc comments in src/rules/require-test-traceability.ts and src/rules/helpers/require-test-traceability-helpers.ts describe: - Configuration options and their semantics. - The exact validation behaviors for file-level annotations, describe blocks, test names, test file detection, and framework compatibility. - These serve as detailed developer-facing documentation, aligning with the story's requirement that rule behavior and configuration options be documented. ,Test execution evidence - Command executed: `npm test -- --ci --no-watch --runInBand --verbose`. - Output (excerpt): - Test suite: "require-test-traceability rule (Stories 020.0 and 021.0)" in tests/rules/require-test-traceability.test.ts reported as PASS with all valid and invalid cases passing. - All 39 test suites and 299 tests passed overall, confirming the stability and correctness of this rule in the context of the full plugin. ,Quality and performance considerations - The rule is built using standard ESLint RuleModule shape with: - Proper meta.schema for option validation (AC: Quality Standards). - Use of context.getFilename, context.getSourceCode, context.report with messageIds, and fixers that modify only comments or string literals, following ESLint best practices. - Performance: - Early exit for non-test files via determineIsTestFile prevents unnecessary work on production code. - Within test files, the rule only: - Scans comments once to check for @supports. - Applies simple regex checks on describe/test names. - Visits CallExpression nodes with minimal work. - There are no file-system operations or heavy computation in this rule; deeper validation of @supports paths and requirement IDs is delegated to existing rules (valid-story-reference, valid-req-reference) that have their own tests and performance constraints. - This design aligns with the story's performance and quality expectations.
traceability.notes: All acceptance criteria for story 020.0-DEV-TEST-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION are implemented and verified: - File-level @supports annotations are required for test files, with a safe, non-semantic auto-fix template when missing (REQ-TEST-FILE-SUPPORTS), and deeper validity of story paths and REQ IDs is handled by existing rules (REQ-TEST-SUPPORTS-VALID via dependencies 005/006/010/010.2). - describe() blocks in test files are validated against a configurable story pattern, with clear errors when missing (REQ-TEST-DESCRIBE-STORY), and this applies to all describe levels, satisfying nested describe handling (REQ-TEST-NESTED-DESCRIBE). - it()/test() names must start with a [REQ-...] prefix; malformed prefixes are normalized where possible while preserving quotes, and missing prefixes are reported with actionable error messages (REQ-TEST-IT-REQ-PREFIX, REQ-TEST-ERROR-CONTEXT in the sense of clear, example-driven guidance). - Test file detection and framework compatibility are implemented via configurable path patterns and support for describe, it, test, and context call names, with dedicated tests covering context() and non-test-file scenarios (REQ-TEST-PATTERN-DETECT, REQ-TEST-FRAMEWORK-COMPAT). - The rule is fully integrated into the plugin’s dynamic rule loading and recommended/strict configurations, and specific integration tests confirm its registration and severity settings. - Documentation exists at both user level (README bullet describing behavior and linking to the user guide) and developer level (comprehensive JSDoc in the rule and helper), covering behavior and configuration options. Given the implemented rule, thorough unit tests, plugin integration, and documented behavior aligned with the story, this story is assessed as fully implemented: PASSED.
